For a fixed \(a\), valid \(k\) satisfy \(k\equiv 1\pmod{a+1}\), so
\[
f(a)=\left\lfloor \frac{\lfloor 60/a\rfloor-1}{a+1}\right\rfloor+1.
\]

Compute the small cases:
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(1)&=30,\\
f(2)&=10,\\
f(3)&=5,\\
f(4)&=3,\\
f(5)&=2,\\
f(6)&=2.
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(a\ge 7\), we have \(\lfloor 60/a\rfloor\le 8\), so
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{\lfloor 60/a\rfloor-1}{a+1}\right\rfloor=0,
\]
hence \(f(a)=1\). There are \(60-7+1=54\) such values of \(a\).

Thus the total number of pairs is
\[
30+10+5+3+2+2+54=106.
\]
\[
\boxed{106}
\]
